chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Whoever did not fast in Dhū al-Ḥijjah until the crescent of al-Muḥarram is sighted, then a sheep-sacrifice is due upon him, and there is no fasting for him, and he should slaughter at Minā.

key_terms.بِمِنًى: at Minā, the ritual location where the slaughter is to take place
key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: the blood-sacrifice of a sheep, meaning a sheep must be offered
key_terms.ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: Dhū al-Ḥijjah, the month in which the prescribed fasting period mentioned here occurs
key_terms.صَوْمٌ: fasting, here as a substitute for sacrificial offering
key_terms.هِلَالُ الْمُحَرَّمِ: the new moon of Muḥarram marking the end of the relevant fasting period
key_terms.يُهَلَّ: the new crescent is sighted or appears

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person delays the compensatory fasting of Dhū al-Ḥijjah until Muḥarram begins?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning one who was required to fast in place of sacrificial offering during hajj but did not complete that fasting before the beginning of Muḥarram. It states that fasting is no longer valid as a substitute in that case, and instead a sheep-sacrifice becomes due, to be slaughtered at Minā.
